# ADR-001: Move the cart store from Redis to Valkey

Status: accepted · Decided: 2024-06-13 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #1619.

## Context
The cart service keeps every shopping cart in a Redis container (redis-cart). In March 2024 Redis changed its licence from BSD to a dual source-available licence (RSALv2/SSPL). We only want to ship OSI-licensed components, and the Linux Foundation fork Valkey is wire-compatible with Redis 7.2.

## Decision
Replace Redis with Valkey for the cart store. Rename the container to valkey-cart, rename RedisCartStore to ValkeyCartStore in cart, and keep the StackExchange.Redis client, which works unchanged against Valkey. Done in #1619 "[Valkey] Replace Redis with Valkey" by Juliano Costa.

## Consequences
No change to the cart's data model or client library. The collector's redis receiver keeps scraping valkey-cart. Operators must use valkey-cli instead of redis-cli. Carts are still not persisted: losing valkey-cart loses carts, which is acceptable for the shop (see the follow-up ticket on persistence).

## Pull requests
- #1619 [Valkey] Replace Redis with Valkey (Juliano Costa)
props.title: ADR-001: Move the cart store from Redis to Valkey

# ADR-002: Serve the product catalogue from PostgreSQL (astronomy-db)

Status: accepted · Decided: 2025-12-29 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #2859, #3153, #3577.

## Context
product-catalog used to read products from a JSON file baked into the image. That made the catalogue impossible to change at runtime and gave us no realistic database telemetry or database failure modes to demonstrate.

## Decision
Store products in the `catalog` schema of astronomy-db (PostgreSQL) and query them from product-catalog (#2859 "[product-catalog] use database for products"), with dedicated application and monitoring users (#3153 "More realistic PostgreSQL setup with dedicated users, database, and monitoring"). Instrument the queries with otelsql (#3577 "feat(product-catalog): Add otelsql SQLCommenter instrumentation").

## Consequences
product-catalog now depends on astronomy-db; a slow database slows the home page, recommendations and checkout. Query telemetry must not break plan reuse (see INC-2026-035). Monitoring runs as monitoring_user with pg_monitor.

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-08-29 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #3873, #4022.

## Context

# ADR-005: Publish orders to Kafka and make every consumer idempotent

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-03-30 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #3219, #3504, #3665.

## Context
checkout publishes each placed order to the Kafka `orders` topic; accounting and fraud-detection consume it. Kafka gives at-least-once delivery, so restarts and rebalances redeliver messages.

## Decision
Keep Kafka as the only channel from checkout to back-office consumers, configured through KAFKA_ADDR / KAFKA_TOPIC (#3219 "fix/add KAFKA_ADDR env var", #3665 "Add KAFKA_TOPIC environment variable"). Consumers must be idempotent: accounting deduplicates by order id (#3504 "fix(accounting): handle duplicate order from Kafka redelivery").

## Consequences
checkout's PlaceOrder does not wait for accounting. Consumer lag is the main health signal for orders-data (see INC-2026-036).

## Pull requests
- #3219 fix/add KAFKA_ADDR env var (Juliano Costa)
- #3504 fix(accounting): handle duplicate order from Kafka redelivery (Matthew Wimpelberg)
- #3665 Add KAFKA_TOPIC environment variable (Ryan Faircloth)
props.title: ADR-005: Publish orders to Kafka and make every consumer idempotent

# ADR-006: Inject demo failures through flagd feature flags, not code branches

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-01-05 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #2830, #3305, #3625, #3931.

## Context
The shop exists to demonstrate incidents. Failure modes used to be hard-coded or required redeploys.

## Decision
Every failure scenario is a flagd flag in src/flagd/demo.flagd.json with a generated OpenFeature client (#3305 "refactor: add OpenFeature flag generation support with checkout and product-catalog services"): cart readiness (#2830 "Add Grpc Readiness probe to cart microservice. Failure can be enabled through feature flag to simulate pod not ready situation"), cart failure rate (#3625 "Make cartFailure rate configurable instead of a fixed toggle"), product-catalog lock contention (#3931 "Add database lock contention scenario to flagd (productCatalogLockContention)"). Defaults are always off.

## Consequences
Anyone can trigger or stop a scenario from flagd-ui. A wrong default ships an outage (see INC-2026-040), so flag defaults get a second reviewer.

- #3305 refactor: add OpenFeature flag generation support with checkout and product-catalog services (Roman Dmytrenko)

# ADR-007: Run checkout, product-catalog and shipping with a read-only root filesystem

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-07-03 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #3658.

## Context
The Go and Rust services never need to write to their image filesystem; a writable root makes container escapes and accidental state easier.

## Decision
Set read_only: true with a tmpfs for /tmp on checkout, product-catalog and shipping (#3658 "Run checkout, product-catalog, and shipping with a read-only root filesystem").

## Consequences

# ADR-008: Export OTLP over http/protobuf from checkout and shipping

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-06-26 · Synthetic ADR written for the Blastradius demo, grounded in real PRs: #3618, #3619.

## Context
gRPC exporters pulled a large dependency tree into small services and were harder to route through proxies.

## Decision
Switch checkout (#3618 "Migrate checkout OTLP exporters from gRPC to http/protobuf") and shipping (#3619 "Migrate shipping OTLP exporters from gRPC to http/protobuf") to the http/protobuf OTLP exporter.

## Consequences
Smaller binaries, but the http exporter's buffers need memory headroom; checkout's 20 MiB limit was too tight (INC-2026-037). Set GOMEMLIMIT on Go services.

## Pull requests
- #3618 Migrate checkout OTLP exporters from gRPC to http/protobuf (Cijo Thomas)
- #3619 Migrate shipping OTLP exporters from gRPC to http/protobuf (Cijo Thomas)

props.rootCause: The new cart health check calls Valkey synchronously with a 2 s timeout and no start period. During a valkey-cart restart the check failed three times in a row, the orchestrator killed cart, and the restarts kept valkey-cart's connection backlog high.
props.summary: After #3487 "[chore] Add health check to services" added container health checks, cart was marked unhealthy and restarted whenever valkey-cart took more than a few seconds to accept connections. The storefront's cart page returned 503 for 38 minutes; checkout could not read carts.
props.title: cart restart loop: new health check fails while valkey-cart warms up

props.rootCause: NODE_OPTIONS required the auto-instrumentation register module from a path that did not exist in the slimmed production image, so `node` exited before opening the gRPC port; the health check never passed.
props.summary: #3486 "feat(payment): use zero-code JS instrumentation via NODE_OPTIONS" moved payment to zero-code JS instrumentation loaded through NODE_OPTIONS. New payment pods crashed on start, so every checkout charge failed for 22 minutes until the deployment was rolled back. The permanent fix landed later in #3844 "Fix payment service not starting and failing health checks".
props.title: payment fails to start after switching to zero-code instrumentation

props.rootCause: The stdout layer buffered formatted events in memory before flushing; with debug-level filtering left on, the buffer grew faster than it drained inside the 20 MiB container limit.
props.summary: #3572 "feat(shipping): add stdout log layer" added a stdout log layer to shipping. Under the load test shipping wrote every span event to stdout, hit its 20 MiB memory limit and was OOM-killed every few minutes. checkout saw intermittent GetQuote/ShipOrder errors for about an hour.
props.title: shipping OOM-killed after stdout log layer doubled log volume

props.rootCause: SQLCommenter appends the trace context to every query, so each statement text became unique. astronomy-db stopped reusing prepared plans and pg_stat_statements churned through entries; under load the catalog queries queued behind planning.
props.summary: After #3577 "feat(product-catalog): Add otelsql SQLCommenter instrumentation" enabled otelsql SQLCommenter in product-catalog, ListProducts p99 rose from 40 ms to 2.4 s. The home page and recommendations slowed down for 70 minutes; checkout's product lookups timed out occasionally.
props.title: product-catalog p99 latency 2.4s after SQLCommenter instrumentation

props.rootCause: Offsets were committed only on a timer; the hosted service's StopAsync did not commit before disposing the consumer, so restarts re-delivered several minutes of orders.
props.summary: After #3608 "fix(accounting): run consumer as hosted service" ran the accounting consumer as a hosted service, the consumer stopped committing offsets on shutdown. Each deploy replayed the orders topic from the last commit; lag peaked at 40k messages and duplicate rows appeared in accounting.order until the dedupe from #3504 "fix(accounting): handle duplicate order from Kafka redelivery" caught up.
props.title: accounting consumer lag 40k on orders after hosted-service change

props.rootCause: The http exporter keeps a larger retry queue and serialises batches into fresh buffers; with GOMEMLIMIT unset the Go runtime let the heap grow past the container's 20 MiB limit during export bursts.
props.summary: #3618 "Migrate checkout OTLP exporters from gRPC to http/protobuf" moved checkout's OTLP exporters from gRPC to http/protobuf. Under the Saturday load test checkout (20 MiB limit) was OOM-killed repeatedly and frontend showed PlaceOrder errors for 9% of orders over 50 minutes.
props.title: checkout OOM-killed after OTLP exporter migration to http/protobuf

props.rootCause: The mobile app builds absolute image URLs from the API response; a relative `/images/...` path resolved against the app bundle origin instead of frontend-proxy.
props.summary: #3582 "fix(frontend): simplify image loader to always return a relative URL" made the frontend image loader always return a relative URL. Browsers were fine behind frontend-proxy, but react-native-app clients resolved the URLs against the wrong host and showed no product images for half a day.
props.title: product images missing in the mobile app after image loader change

props.rootCause: The new flag variant map had the 10% variant as defaultVariant; nobody noticed because the old boolean flag defaulted to off.
props.summary: #3625 "Make cartFailure rate configurable instead of a fixed toggle" turned the cartFailure flag from an on/off toggle into a failure rate. The default variant in demo.flagd.json shipped as a 10% rate instead of 0, so EmptyCart failed for one in ten checkouts for three hours.
props.title: cart EmptyCart failures at 10% after cartFailure became a rate

props.rootCause: The fix flipped the default branch: with IPV6_ENABLED unset the server listened on [::] without dual-stack, which the IPv4-only CNI did not route.
props.summary: After #3741 "fix(currency): correct IPV6_ENABLED string comparison" corrected the IPV6_ENABLED comparison, currency bound only to the IPv6 wildcard on an IPv4-only staging cluster. frontend and checkout could not convert prices for 35 minutes.

steps: Describe the group: `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group accounting`.
Make sure the kafkaQueueProblems and kafkaConsumerDead flags are off in flagd-ui.
Restart accounting once (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/accounting`) and watch lag drain.
Check astronomy-db for duplicates: `SELECT order_id, count(*) FROM accounting."order" GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1;`.
props.title: accounting consumer lag on orders

steps: Open flagd-ui (/feature via frontend-proxy) and check cartFailure; set it to the `off` variant.
Make the change permanent in src/flagd/demo.flagd.json (defaultVariant: off) and redeploy flagd.
Confirm cart error rate falls to zero within a minute; valkey-cart needs no action.
props.title: cart errors caused by the cartFailure flag

steps: Check restarts and the last state: `kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/component=cart` (compose: `docker compose ps cart`).
Check valkey-cart first: `kubectl exec deploy/valkey-cart -- valkey-cli ping` must return PONG.
If valkey-cart is healthy but cart keeps restarting, relax the cart healthcheck (start_period 20s, timeout 5s) in compose.yaml / the Helm values and redeploy.
Restart in order: valkey-cart, then cart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/cart`.
Verify in Grafana (Demo dashboard, cart panel) that GetCart errors are back under 1% and checkout PlaceOrder recovers.
props.title: cart restart loop / unhealthy

steps: Check restarts: `kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/component=checkout`; `describe` shows OOMKilled.
Roll back: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout` and confirm PlaceOrder errors drop.
Mitigate: set GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB and raise the memory limit to 40M for checkout in compose.yaml / Helm values.
Check the downstream calls are healthy: cart, payment, shipping, currency, email and the kafka orders topic.
Verify on the Demo dashboard that checkout's p99 and error rate are back to baseline.
props.title: checkout OOMKilled / PlaceOrder errors

steps: Check what currency listens on: `kubectl exec deploy/currency -- ss -ltn`.
Set IPV6_ENABLED=false explicitly on deployment/currency and restart.
Verify frontend price rendering and checkout PlaceOrder recover.
props.title: currency unreachable

steps: Request an image through the proxy: `curl -I http://frontend-proxy:8080/images/products/<file>`; 200 means image-provider is fine.
Check image-provider nginx status: `curl http://image-provider:8081/status`; the imageSlowLoad flag must be off.
If only clients are affected, roll back frontend: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend`.
props.title: product images missing

steps: Read the first log lines of a new pod: `kubectl logs deploy/payment --previous`; a `Cannot find module` error means the NODE_OPTIONS --require path is wrong.
Roll back immediately: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/payment`; confirm checkout PlaceOrder succeeds.
To keep payment up while debugging, unset NODE_OPTIONS on the deployment; telemetry is lost but charges work.
Check the paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable flags are off in flagd-ui so they do not mask the real cause.
Before re-rolling, build the image locally and run `node --require <path> index.js` to prove the module resolves.
props.title: payment crash-loops on start

steps: Look at astronomy-db: `SELECT calls, mean_exec_time, query FROM pg_stat_statements ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC LIMIT 10;` (connect as monitoring_user).
Check `pg_stat_activity` for waiting queries and locks on the catalog schema; the productCatalogLockContention flag must be off.
If query texts differ only by a trailing comment, disable SQLCommenter on deployment/product-catalog and restart it.
Watch the PostgreSQL dashboard in Grafana until mean_exec_time is back to baseline.
If astronomy-db stays saturated, restart product-catalog pods one by one to drop their connection pools.
props.title: product-catalog slow / astronomy-db saturated

steps: Confirm the reason: `kubectl describe pod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=shipping` shows `OOMKilled`.
Lower log volume: set RUST_LOG=info on deployment/shipping and restart.
If still OOM, roll back shipping: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/shipping`.
Check checkout's shipping errors drop on the Demo dashboard; quote should be unaffected.
props.title: shipping OOMKilled

props.text:
Diogo Pacheco: New-ish question: why did we move the cart cache from Redis to Valkey? Was it performance?
Juliano Costa: Not performance. Redis changed its licence in 2024 to a source-available one, and we only ship OSI-licensed components. Valkey is the Linux Foundation fork and speaks the same protocol, so #1619 "[Valkey] Replace Redis with Valkey" was basically an image swap plus renaming RedisCartStore to ValkeyCartStore.
Florian Bourgey: And the cart code didn't change: StackExchange.Redis talks to Valkey fine. It's written up in ADR-001.
Diogo Pacheco: So the move to Valkey was about the licence. Is valkey-cart persisted?
Juliano Costa: No, still in-memory only; there's a ticket about persistence after INC-2026-031.
props.title: Why is the cart on Valkey and not Redis?

props.text:
Matthew Wimpelberg: Proposing to revert the load generator from k6 back to Locust. We lost the Locust web UI, the flood-homepage flag and the Python span attributes the dashboards use.
Cijo Thomas: Wasn't the whole reason for k6 the gevent greenlet crashes in Locust?
Diogo Pacheco: I can fix that with a gRPC/gevent compatibility flag; that's cheaper than rebuilding every scenario in k6.
Matthew Wimpelberg: Then let's go back to Locust. Writing ADR-004 to supersede ADR-003; the revert is #3873.
props.title: k6 vs Locust: why did we revert the load generator?

props.text:
Antonin Bruneau: Postmortem for INC-2026-035: SQLCommenter made every query text unique. I'd like to keep the trace links, though.
Piotr Kiełkowicz: Keep it off by default and only enable it when the flag is on. ADR-002 says telemetry must not break plan reuse.
Diogo Pacheco: Agreed. I'll add a PostgreSQL dashboard panel so we see plan churn before customers do.
props.title: Do we keep SQLCommenter on product-catalog?

props.text:
Matthew Wimpelberg: We're seeing duplicate orders in accounting after Kafka redeliveries. Should we turn on transactions / exactly-once?
Cijo Thomas: Exactly-once across Kafka and Postgres is a lot of machinery for a demo shop. Dedupe on order id is simpler.
Matthew Wimpelberg: OK: idempotent consumers it is. Writing it down in ADR-005; fix is #3504.
props.title: Exactly-once vs idempotent consumers for orders

props.text:
Cijo Thomas: INC-2026-037 was my exporter change, #3618. The http exporter needs more buffer than 20M allows.
